_README: THE SCORING MODEL. Edit this file, not the score.
Every item is one concrete deliverable with a WEIGHT in body-of-work units
(roughly: how much of this project's effort it is/was) and a VALUE in 0..1.
A section's score is the weighted mean of its items. The overall score is the
An item's value comes from exactly one of two places, and the difference is
the whole point of this file:
"value": n      -- ATTESTED. A human confirmed it. `evidence` must say how.
"probe": "..."  -- MEASURED. score.py computes it from the tree every run.
⚠ THE ONE RULE: never raise an attested value because something LOOKS done.
Raise it when a run on real hardware confirmed it, and put the run in
`evidence`. This project's most expensive bugs have all been things that
read as working -- see docs/STATE.md, `a stepped-over call still answers`.
⚠ THE BAR IS 'ntvdm SUPERSET ON XP-32', ONE BAR, FOR EVERY SECTION. It is NOT
the DOS games bar. Doom and Skyroads being playable is two items here, not a
score of 85. Scoring the halves against different bars is how the 2026-09-04
review got a headline of 65 that its own components did not support.

epic #24 'BIOS complete', 15 probes clean; INT 13h scored separately ★ s54: INT 10h AH=01h CURSOR EMULATION, which is a real BIOS behaviour we simply did not have. DOS asks for its cursor in scan lines of an EIGHT-line character cell (underline = 6-7, insert block = 0-7) because that is the machine it was written for; our cell is 16 lines, so honouring those numbers literally put the underline HALFWAY UP -- rendered as `ABC123-` where a real DOS box shows `ABC123_`. Reported by the user, and it was our own default doing it too (cur_shape init 0x0607). Fixed with the VGA BIOS's own scaling rule (IBM's, as carried by Bochs/SeaBIOS) reproduced rather than approximated -- an approximation here is a cursor a pixel out on every DOS prompt in existence. 6-7 -> 14-15, 0-7 -> 1-15. 9 off-VM checks pinning the exact shapes DOS uses, including the adjacent-line branch that keeps the underline TWO lines instead of smearing it to three. CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE for the overwrite underline, at a real COMMAND.COM prompt. ⚠ NOT confirmed for the insert block: the synthetic keys never reached the guest in that run, and plain COMMAND.COM may not set 0x0007 at all -- it is DOSKEY and full-screen editors that do. Implemented and unit-tested, not yet witnessed.

#133 CLOSED s52 -- oracle, rig AND stock ntvdm agree on all six cases. #131 STILL NOT CLOSED, but s54 turned it from a blocked decision into a LOCATED BUG. (1) THE RECORDED HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED: `we are a GUI-subsystem binary where stock ntvdm is console` is simply false -- our PE subsystem is already CUI, pinned deliberately in CMakeLists.txt. (2) A FIFTH ROUTE was tried and eliminated: VDM_COMMAND_INFO carries StdIn/StdOut/StdErr at +0x10, which is how stock gets a console it never inherited; ours come back as non-handles (0x02341fc0/0x7c867f23/0x65470000, identical every run, all three FILE_TYPE_UNKNOWN). (3) THE INSTRUMENT THAT SAID SO NAMED THE REAL DEFECT: the WHOLE struct is junk -- CreationFlags 0x4d445674 and CodePage 0x78654e74 are ASCII and constant, AppName is garbage, TaskId is 0 -- so GetNextVDMCommand returns TRUE and populates NOTHING. We never noticed because the launch does not depend on it (the program comes from target.txt or our own command line). And the command line says why: it arrives as `-f` with NO -i<taskid>, so CSRSS cannot tell which queued task we are asking about. The shape that DOES carry -i (anything through `start`, which is every run rt.bat has ever done) reports TaskId 0x18 and gets `inherited console` -- which is exactly how this stayed invisible for fifty sessions. ==> #131 IS THE SAME DEFECT AS THE M2.5 ITEM `recover the real command line from CSRSS's undocumented multi-call protocol`; fixing one fixes both. (4) AND THE TARGET IS PROVEN REACHABLE, by the oracle rather than by argument: `hello.com > out.txt` typed at cmd writes 136 bytes under STOCK ntvdm on the same box and 0 bytes under ours. Live streaming is wired and works the moment a handle exists; what is missing is the handshake, not the plumbing.

CLOSED s53, rig-gated and diffed against stock. ROOT CAUSE: MS Paint takes the mouse capture on button-down and NEVER gives it back -- nine SetCapture and ZERO ReleaseCapture in one measured session, and it RE-TAKES it after every button-up. That is legal Win16, but USER32 refuses SC_KEYMENU while the calling thread holds a capture (menus deliberately do not open mid-drag), so DefWindowProc did nothing with Alt and the menu bar was dead for the rest of the session. ★ THE FIX IS WHAT STOCK IS OBSERVED TO DO, not an invention: cross-process GetGUIThreadInfo (new `rigshot capture` verb) shows stock ALSO leaves the capture on the canvas after three drags, and Alt MOVES it to the top-level window and enters GUI_INMENUMODE. We now do the same on WM_SYSKEYDOWN for VK_MENU/VK_F10, and only when one of OUR windows holds it. ★ WHY STOCK GETS IT FREE: its thread reports GUI_16BITTASK (flags 0x20), ours reports 0 -- USER32 gives its own WOW threads special menu handling and that flag is not settable from outside. VERIFIED: after three canvas drags, menuowner set and flags=0x04 (GUI_INMENUMODE), and the File menu is open in the screenshot with the drawn stroke visible behind it -- docs/research/evidence/session53-menu-after-drags.png.

#136 s53/s54, RIG-GATED on 192.168.1.29: 24 of 47 rows are live, up from 7. s54 ADDS THE ONE THE OLD NOTE CALLED OUT BY NAME -- `the whole CPU page needs a duty-cycle throttle on the exec loop (there are no cycles to count on a real CPU)`. SpeedMode is no longer the dead DOSBox-vocabulary combo (Auto|Maximum|Fixed cycles); it is the approximate-speed dropdown of GH #56, Unlimited|200|100|66|33|16|8 MHz, on the Settings CPU page AND as a radio submenu under Machine, both backed by one registry value. Old values migrate: index 0 meant `do nothing` before and still does. MECHANISM: the exec thread is SUSPENDED for a share of each period -- the same SuspendThread/GetThreadContext/ResumeThread machinery async_inject_irq has used for twenty sessions -- gated on g_in_exec so a lock holder can never be stopped; the mode-12h interpreter paces itself by instruction budget instead. MEASURED ON HARDWARE, four sweeps of tools/dostest/cpubench.asm (a loop costing 12 cycles on a 486, so MHz comes from a period CPU's published timings rather than a guess): unthrottled 3665 MHz apparent; 100 MHz -> 103 measured; 200 -> 305; 66 -> 89; 33 -> 73; and the two slowest SATURATE, which the host LOGS as delivered_mhz beside the requested one rather than pretending. 36 new off-VM checks. THREE MECHANISMS WERE MEASURED WRONG BEFORE THIS ONE WAS RIGHT, and each was wrong in a way that looked like success: a per-millisecond Bresenham gave 6x where 87x was asked (the Suspend/Resume cost ate each 1 ms hold); sleeping the off-period whether or not the hold LANDED let the guest run free half the time and made the sweep NON-MONOTONIC; and pricing the hold off the 1 ms we ASK for rather than the run phase actually measured came out 3.5x fast at every setting. Selftest stays 8/8 and at Unlimited every throttle counter reads zero, so the default is the old behaviour exactly. GAPS: CpuType/CpuCore/Fpu/Cycles/Turbo are still scaffold; ConventionalKB/Umb need DOS_MEM_TOP to stop being a compile-time constant; Renderer needs a windowed DirectDraw blit that does not exist; Opl needs an OPL3 that does not exist. And the honest cost: a slow setting is CHUNKY -- 1 ms of running per ~110 ms held at 33 MHz -- because 1 ms is the smallest unit Sleep can hand out. NOT YET USER-JUDGED: whether the five speed-affected demos FEEL period-correct, which is #56's own acceptance bar and needs eyes on the box. CAVE was launched and left running for that; note it is the VSYNC-paced one, so MATRIX_1 (delay-loop) and BUBBLES (unpaced) are the sharper tests. ★ s54: THE WHOLE DISPLAY PAGE IS NOW ALSO ON THE VIEW MENU, and the two routes mean different things on purpose -- the dialog edits the SAVED configuration, the menu changes only what is in force and never writes the registry, so a scaler or a speed tried while watching something run is gone at the next launch (rig-proven: WindowSize picked twice from the menu, registry still 0x0 after). CPU Speed moved to the same rule. ⚠ AND `WindowSize is live` WAS AN OVERCLAIM IN THE LINE ABOVE: it was read ONCE just before CreateWindow, so changing it did nothing you could see until the next launch -- reported by the user as `I tried display size and it didn't resize`, which is exactly what it did. Now it resizes the live window, measured on hardware both ways: client 640x423 -> 1280x823 -> 640x423. That fix also exposed a REAL DEFECT hiding behind a compile-time constant: PRESENT_STATUS_H guesses the status bar at 22px and comctl32 makes it 23, so the client area was a pixel short of the framebuffer and the guest lost a row of picture at EVERY scale, invisible until 1x came back one pixel taller than it started. The window is now sized to the control's measured height. Renderer is STILL read by nothing -- GDI is the only windowed path and DirectDraw is fullscreen-only, with no Direct3D or OpenGL code anywhere in src/; its four entries are listed enabled per the standing scaffold-stub decision. ★★ s54 SECOND PASS, all rig-gated: AspectRatio stopped being a checkbox and became an ASPECT LOCK -- None/4:3/16:9/16:10 -- which constrains the window's shape while it is dragged (WM_SIZING) so the picture fills the client instead of being letterboxed inside a free-shaped one; letterboxing survives only for the cases the lock cannot reach, such as maximised. The window base is now `the smallest client this aspect allows` rather than the 640x400 TEXT framebuffer, which was only one of the shapes a guest runs in and is not even 4:3. MEASURED, video area in every case 480 tall: None 640x480, 4:3 640x480, 16:10 768x480, 16:9 853x480 -- the 640x480 floor, with the height binding first for anything wider than 4:3. ⚠ MY FIRST 16:9 MINIMUM WAS 854x481, a pixel proud on BOTH axes because width and height were ceiling-rounded independently instead of letting one constraint bind and deriving the other; caught by a test written from the numbers quoted to the user before the code existed. Window scales that cannot fit the desktop work area are now GREYED rather than silently substituted (3x is dead on a 1680x1050 desktop) -- not the scaffold-stub case, because that item is implemented and physically impossible on this display. The CPU ladder went 7 -> 18 entries up to 3300 MHz, which renumbered the registry indices: taken deliberately, documented, and the permanent fix (store MHz, not an index) is written down. Status strip: the name part is measured in the control's own font so the divider sits just after the name, instead of reserving widths from the right edge and stranding the machine state mid-strip.

#130 s52: target.txt no longer overrides unconditionally. ★ s53 THE INSTALL/UNINSTALL FLOW IS NOW VERIFIED ON HARDWARE, AND BEHAVIOURALLY RATHER THAN BY THE REGISTRY VALUE -- a key that reads correctly and does not route is the failure this project has been bitten by. installcycle.bat: (1) delete the Debugger value, run a DOS program -> NO host log, so stock ran it; (2) add the value back, run THE SAME program -> host log present, so ours ran it; (3) delete and re-add, proving the key each time. That is the stated gap closed. ★ AND WIN16 COVERAGE IS 9 GUESTS, NOT 5: NOTEPAD, PBRUSH, SYSEDIT, SOL, WINMINE, CLOCK, RECORDER, CHARMAP, MPLAYER have all been routed through the IFEO hook and put a window on the desktop this session; five are user-confirmed doing their job. (The gap this line used to name -- `there is still no INSTALLER` -- is closed; see below.) ★★★ s54: THERE IS AN INSTALLER, which is exactly the gap this line named. `ntvdmhost.exe /install`, `/uninstall`, `/status` -- and the same three on the File menu with a confirmation, because it changes a machine-wide setting that outlives the process. It CHECKS FOR AN EXISTING VALUE and it CAN PUT IT BACK: a Debugger value belonging to another program is SAVED before we displace it and RESTORED on uninstall, and one we never installed is REFUSED rather than deleted -- deleting it would break a tool we cannot even name afterwards. Every claim is verified by reading the value back and re-classifying it, not by a return code. 21 off-VM checks on the decision itself (quoted vs unquoted, case, trailing space, forward slashes, a path that merely starts with ours). RIG-GATED BEHAVIOURALLY, all six cases: /uninstall then run a DOS program -> NO host log (stock ran it); /install then run the same program -> host log present (ours ran it); /install twice -> `already`; REFUSE leaves a foreign value byte-for-byte unchanged; RESTORE puts it back. ⚠ AND THE RIG CAUGHT A BUG THE REGISTRY READ COULD NOT: the first cut computed `want = (verb != 2)`, so /uninstall asked to be INSTALLED and cheerfully reported `INSTALLED` while doing it -- the message being composed from the same wrong flag. Only the behavioural half found it. GAP, and it is why this is not 1.0: there is no PACKAGE -- no setup that copies the exe somewhere sensible, makes a Start Menu entry or uninstalls through Add/Remove Programs. The routing half is done; the shipping half is not.

#9 s56. src/vdd/vdd_comm.c is a real 8250/16550A -- RBR/THR, IER, IIR/FCR, LCR, MCR, LSR, MSR, SCR, the divisor latch behind DLAB, a 256-byte receive ring, IRQ4/3 gated on OUT2 -- plus the parallel side's data/status/control at 0x378, where the byte is emitted on the RISING EDGE OF STROBE. The gap was never `INT 14h is missing`: it answered since GH #45, but 0x3F8.. was UNCLAIMED (so a guest driving the hardware read 0xFF from every register), receive returned TIMEOUT unconditionally because there was nothing to receive from, and transmit wrote to g_serial -- THE HOST'S OWN DEBUG CHANNEL. INT 14h is now claimed BY the VDD, so the BIOS and the registers cannot disagree, and the equipment word is COMPUTED from the VDD (both INT 11h arms had a comment claiming `one serial` over a constant whose serial bits were 0). MEASURED off-VM 55/55 (tools/dostest/comm_test.c, built around local loopback because that is the one part of a UART establishable with no peer or cable) and ON THE RIG (tools/dostest/comport.asm): EQUIP=4421 SER=2, BDA COM1=03F8, SCRATCH OK, LOOP TX=5A RX=5A OK, DTR>DSR / RTS>CTS / OUT1>RI / OUT2>DCD all OK, BIOS14 TX=5A RX=5A OK, LPT1 STATUS=D8 OK -- and both spools on the box hold what the guest sent. GAPS, and they are why this is not 1.0: transmit goes to a SPOOL FILE only, with no passthrough to a real \\.\COMn and no settings UI to choose; COM3/COM4 and LPT2/LPT3 are not fitted; baud is stored but paces nothing (deliberate, see the header); and no guest has yet been driven through it end to end -- TERMINAL's Default Serial Port dialog is the obvious next test.
